data.name: Janardhan
data.gender_notes: Janardhan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Janardhan is a popular Hindu name, derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'Lord of the World'. In Hindu mythology, Janardhan is a form of Lord Vishnu, who is revered as the sustainer and protector of the universe. The name evokes a sense of strength, power, and divine presence. The name Janardhan carries the meaning “Lord of the World” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Janardhan usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the world and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine presence and the power to sustain and protect.
data.etymology: Janardhan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the World.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Janardhan total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

The name carries an important symbolic meaning, reminding the people of their connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: Janardhan is believed to be an embodiment of love, compassion, and protection. For many devotees, invoking the name of Janardhan brings a sense of peace, comfort, and strength. It is a reminder of the divine presence that sustains and protects the universe, and the faith that one's prayers will be answered.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Janardhan symbolizes the all-pervading Lord who is the source of all desires and attachments. The name embodies the concept of Hari (Vishnu) as the one who fulfills all needs and removes all sorrows.

vedic_reference.note: Janardana is a form of Vishnu, who is the protector of the common man and the upholder of dharma.

historical_references.reference: Janardhan is a name for the Hindu deity Vishnu, particularly in his Dwadash Lakshmi form, which represents the twelve main aspects of Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity. Janardhan means 'the one who gives pleasure to Jana, or people'.
historical_references.time_period: Throughout Hindu history, particularly from the medieval period onwards
historical_references.context: The name is used in various Hindu scriptures, mythological stories, and daily religious practices.

historical_references.reference: Another reference for Janardhan is found in the Mahabharata, where it is mentioned that Arjuna, one of the Pandava brothers, worshipped Lord Vishnu as Janardhan while in the forest during his exile. He sought Lord Vishnu's blessings and guidance to win the great battle of Kurukshetra.
historical_references.context: The Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India.
